newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-SLATER AND PONTING EXPERIENCE CONTRASTING FORTUNES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SLATER AND PONTING EXPERIENCE CONTRASTING FORTUNES.

text.p: Michael Slater and Ricky Ponting, both axed from the Australian side, experienced contrasting fortunes in their Sheffield Shield appearances on Friday.

Opener Slater hit 102, his first century in more than a year, to help New South Wales establish a hefty lead on the second day of their day-night match against South Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
New South Wales were 342 for five at the close, a lead of 188 over the visitors.
Earlier in Hobart, Ponting fell for just eight runs as Tasmania struggled to 288 for eight on the first day of their match against Western Australia.

Ponting was caught at mid-wicket from the fast bowling of Jo Angel on an unpredictable pitch. Opener Jamie Cox was the top scorer with 96 while number three Michael DiVenuto scored 65. Angel was the pick of the Western Australian bowlers with three for 59 from 17 overs.
Slater's century was only the second time he has passed 50 in nine innings since he was dropped from the test team last November, but he said he was always confident his form would return.
"Throughout all this I never felt I was out of nick. I never felt gee I've lost it with the bat," Slater said.
Three hours play was lost due to rain after lunch and the rain again forced the players off the field 10 minutes before the close.
Slater's overnight partner Kevin Roberts hit his maiden first class century with a stylish 119.
